parameters.name: Gr Use
parameters.description:
Flag
'Check' the cell if you wish to use the gamma ray log as a clay indicator in this zone.
'Un-check' the cell for 'Vclay gamma ray' to be set to Null values over this zone.

parameters.name: Gr Clean
parameters.description: 'Gamma Ray curve value in a clean, 0%, Vclay zone'.

parameters.name: Gr Clay
parameters.description: 'Gamma Ray curve value in a 100% clay zone'.

parameters.name: Gr Method
parameters.description:
The following methods can be selected
 'Linear' : Linear relationship between GR and VclGr
 'Curved' : A composite, curved relationship
 'Clavier' : As per Clavier et al.
 'Stieber' : As per Stieber et al. (South Louisiana Miocene and Pliocene)
 'Old Rock' : As per Larionov et al. for older (Mesozoic)rocks 
 'Young Rock' : As per Larionov for younger (Tertiary clastic)rocks

parameters.name: Link Clay Paras
parameters.description:
Flag
'Check' the cell / column if you wish a Double Clay parameter that is common to 2 Double Clay Indicators to be updated simultaneously if one clay parameter is changed. 

For example, If 'checked', changing the Neutron/Density Clay Density parameter (ND Den Clay) will update the Sonic/ Density Clay Density parameter (SD Den Clay) with the same value.
'Un-check' the cell / column if you do not wish to link Double Clay Indicator parameters.

parameters.name: Link PhiSw Clay
parameters.description:
Flag
When 'Checked' the 'Density', 'Neutron' and 'Sonic clay' parameters are linked to the equivalent parameters in the PhiSw module.
This also links the 'Neutron/Density clean point 1' 'Density' Parameter to the PhiSw module 'Matrix Density' parameter.
The Clay Volume and PhiSw parameters sets must also be linked for this to work.

parameters.name: Vcl Av Method
parameters.description:
This parameter controls the way the VCLav curve is calculated 
Option are :
 Mean : The mean value of all the individual Vcl curves is taken
 Median : The median value of all the individual Vcl curves is taken
 Lateral : The Lateral average value of all the individual Vcl curves is taken. 
 
The Lateral average is the median value of all the individual pair products. This is almost identical to the Hodges-Lehmann method.

parameters.name: Vcl Mix Method
parameters.description:
The Vclmix output curve allows the mixing of the Vcl minimum and Vcl average curves by zone. The parameter controls the selection.
 Minimum : The Vclmix output curve will be the same as the Vcl minimum curve
 Average : The Vclmix output curve will be the same as the Vcl average curve

parameters.name: Use Percentile
parameters.description:
When ticked the percentiles entered under the 'Percentile Clean' and the 'Percentile Clay' parameters will be used to calculate the 'Gr Clean' and 'Gr Clay' parameters which are used for the calculation of Vcl GammaRay.
 
 If Organic shale corrections are being made then this option to Use Percentiles will become unavailable.

parameters.name: Percentile Clean
parameters.description:
When 'Use Percentile' is ticked this parameter is used to calculate the 'Gr Clean' parameter. Enter the number in %. Numbers can be less than 0%. Negative percentiles are calculated by a linear scaling from the 0% to the 100% percentiles and extrapolating to the negative entered number. 
 
 The Percentile is calculated from the input GammRay curve data for all zones which have the same 'Percentile Group' number as the current zone. Hence if all zones use the same 'Percentile Group' number then a 10th percentile for all zones will give the same Gr Clean for all zones.
 
 When 'Use Percentile' is un-ticked this parameter is calculated from the 'Gr Clean' parameter using the input GammRay curve data for all zones which have the same 'Percentile Group' number as the current zone.

parameters.name: Percentile Clay
parameters.description:
When 'Use Percentile' is ticked this parameter is used to calculate the 'Gr Clay' parameter. Enter the number in %. Numbers greater than 100% are allowed and are normal for the calculation of clay volume. Percentiles over 100% are calculated by a linear scaling from the 0% to the 100% percentiles and extrapolating to the entered number.
 
 The Percentile is calculated from the input GammRay curve data for all zones which have the same 'Percentile Group' number as the current zone. Hence if all zones use the same 'Percentile Group' number then a 90th percentile for all zones will give the same Gr Clay for all zones.
 
 When 'Use Percentile' is un-ticked this parameter is calculated from the 'Gr Clay' parameter using the input GammRay curve data for all zones which have the same 'Percentile Group' number as the current zone.

parameters.name: Percentile Group
parameters.description: The 'Percentile Group' is used for determining which GammRay curve data is used for the percentile calculations or for the lookup of percentiles from 'Gr clean' / 'Gr Clay' parameters when the 'Use Percentile' is un-ticked.

parameters.name: Clip Low %
parameters.description:
The 'Clip Low %' and the 'Clip High %' parameters are used to eliminate spikes in the data which will artificially change the percentiles. Enter a low clip values between 0-100%.
 
 The GammaRay curve data for each 'Percentile Group' is clipped using the 'Clip Low %' and the 'Clip High %' parameters before the percentiles are calculated. This allows a percentile of say 130% to be calculated with the removal of spikes in the data before the 130% is calculated.

parameters.name: Clip High %
parameters.description:
The 'Clip Low %' and the 'Clip High %' parameters are used to eliminate spikes in the data which will artificially change the percentiles. Enter a high clip values between 0-100%.
 
 The GammaRay curve data for each 'Percentile Group' is clipped using the 'Clip Low %' and the 'Clip High %' parameters before the percentiles are calculated.

parameters.name: Stieber Constant
parameters.description:
When the 'Gr Method' parameter is set to 'Stieber' then this constant (default 2.0) is used to control the shape of the curve in the Stieber equation.
 
 VcGr = Z / (1 + STB (1 - Z))
 Where Z is linear Vclay gamma ray and STB is the Stieber constant.

parameters.name: Organic Shale_Corr.
parameters.description: When checked the Vclay Gamma Ray, Vclay Neutron and Vclay Neutron Density will be calculated from the organic shale corrected curves for Gr, Neutron and Density. When unchecked Vclay will be calculated as normal.

parameters.name: Gr Kerogen
parameters.description:
Used to correct the input Gr curve for Kerogen (Uranium). If the input Gr curves is an Uranium corrected curve (eg CGR) then set this value to zero.
 The value is the API reading of 100% Kerogen. 
 
 GrCorr = Gr_in - TOC_in x Kerogen_Wt%Con x Gr_Kerogen 
 Where
 Gr_in = Input Gamma Ray curve
 TOC_in = Input TOC curve in weight percent
 Kerogen_Wt%Con = Conversion factor used to convert input TOC curve in weight % to volumes
 Gr_Kerogen = Gr API reading in 100% Kerogen 
 GrCorr = Output Kerogen corrected Gamma Ray
 
 This value can be obtained from wells where a spectral gamma ray has been run. Crossplot the difference between Normal Gr and Uranium corrected Gr against volume TOC (need to correct TOC from weight % to volume before crossplotting). Make a linear regression through the data and extrapolate the line to 100% TOC. This will be the Gr Kerogen value.

parameters.name: Rhob Kerogen
parameters.description: Density of Kerogen. Default is 1.1 gm/cc

parameters.name: Nphi Kerogen
parameters.description: Neutron of Kerogen. Default is 0.6 v/v

parameters.name: Rhob Heavy_Min.

parameters.name: Nphi Heavy_Min.

parameters.name: Kerogen Wt%_Con.
parameters.description:
Conversion factor to convert input TOC curve in weight % to a volume curve. Default is 2.5 
 
 If the input TOC curve is already in volume then set this factor to 1.0

parameters.name: Heavy_Min. Wt%_Con.
parameters.description:
Conversion factor to convert input Heavy Mineral curve in weight % to a volume curve. Default is 1.0 (input is already in volumes).

parameters.name: Rw
parameters.description: Formation water resistivity.

parameters.description:
'Temperature associated with Rw' - units set on curve input/output screen. The program will convert the Rw to formation temperature using the entered Temperature curve.
If 'Rw Temp' is 'blank' then the Rw will be assumed to be at formation temperature and no further conversion will be made.

If 'Rmf Temp' is 'blank' then the Rmf will be assumed to be at formation temperature and no further conversion will be made.

parameters.name: Rw bound
parameters.description:
'Clay-bound water resistivity'. Used in the 'Dual Water' saturation equation option. 
The value can be estimated from the Rw apparent curve in the shaly wet sections. Rw bound can be adjusted to give 100% Sw in these zones.

parameters.name: Temp Rwb
parameters.description:
'Temperature associated with Rw bound' - units set on curve input/output screen. The program will convert Rw bound to formation temperature using the entered Temperature curve.
If 'Rw bound Temp' is 'blank' then Rw bound will be assumed to be at formation temperature and no further conversion will be made.

parameters.name: Rmf bound
parameters.description:
'Clay-bound water resistivity'. Used in the 'Dual Water' saturation equation option. Normally the same as Rw bound but can be different due to the different responses of the microresistivity curve & the deep resistivity curve in shaly zones.
The value can be estimated from the Rmf apparent curve in the shaly wet sections. Rmf bound can be adjusted to give 100% Sxo in these zones.

parameters.name: Temp Rmfb
parameters.description:
'Temperature associated with Rmf bound' - units set on curve input/output screen. The program will convert Rmf bound to formation temperature using the entered Temperature curve.
If 'Rwf bound Temp' is 'blank' then Rmf bound will be assumed to be at formation temperature and no further conversion will be made.

parameters.name: Rho Sxo zone
parameters.description:
'Flushed zone water density' in gm/cc. Used in the 'Density' equation for the density of the water seen by the tool.
If 'Rho Sxo zone' is 'blank' the value is calculated from Rmf. 
In oil-based mud 'Rho Sxo' is calculated from Rw if the cell is left 'blank'.

parameters.name: Salin Sxo zone
parameters.description:
'Flushed zone water salinity' in decimal notation (25 KPPM entered as .025). Used for making formation salinity corrections to the neutron and calculate TP water.
If 'Salin Sxo zone' is 'blank', the value is calculated from Rmf. 
In oil-based mud 'Salin Sxo zone' is calculated from Rw if the cell is left 'blank'.

parameters.name: Rho Wet Clay

'Density of Wet Clay' in gm/cc. Used for calculating porosity from the density and calculating Wet Clay Total Porosity if not entered.
Must be entered if a density tool is used.

parameters.name: Rho Dry Clay
parameters.description: 'Density of dry clay' in gm/cc. Used for calculating Clay Total Porosity.

parameters.name: Neu Wet Clay
parameters.description:
'Neutron reading in Wet Clay' in decimals. Used for calculating Neutron Porosity.
Must be entered if a neutron tool is used.

parameters.name: Sonic Wet Clay
parameters.description:
'Sonic reading in Wet Clay' in uSec/ft. Used for calculating Sonic Porosity.
Must be entered if a sonic tool is used.

parameters.name: Res Clay
parameters.description:
'Resistivity of the clay'. Used for the 'Simandoux', 'Modified Simandoux' and 'Indonesian' water saturation equations.
Can be selected interactively from the 'Resistivity vs. Vclay' crossplot.

parameters.name: Rxo Clay
parameters.description:
'Resistivity of the clay seen by the microresistivity tool'. Used for the 'Simandoux', 'Modified Simandoux' and 'Indonesian' water saturation equations for calculating Sxo.
Normally the same as 'Res Clay', but can be different due to the different response of the microresistivity curve and the deep resistivity curve in shaly zones.
Can be selected interactively from the 'Rxo vs. Vclay' crossplot.

parameters.name: Hc Den
parameters.description:
'Hydrocarbon Density' in gm/cc. Used to calculate the apparent hydrocarbon density seen by the Density tool and the apparent hydrocarbon hydrogen Index seen by the Neutron tool.
If using the DENSITY/NEUTRON model and the 'variable hydrocarbon density' flag is set, then 'Hc Den' will be the maximum allowable hydrocarbon density.
If 'Hc Den' is left 'blank', the value defaults to 1.0 gm/cc.

parameters.name: Hc Den Min
parameters.description: 'Minimum allowable hydrocarbon density' in gm/cc. Used only in the DENSITY/NEUTRON model and with the variable hydrocarbon density flag set. This value will set the minimum possible hydrocarbon density.

parameters.name: Neu Hc HI
parameters.description:
'Neutron hydrocarbon hydrogen index' in decimals. If you want to override the default calculation, enter the value here, otherwise it will be calculated from the HC Den parameter.
Default calculation is 'Neu Hc HI' = RhoH * 9 (4 - 2.5 RhoH) / (16 - 2.5 RhoH)
where RhoH is the input hydrocarbon density (Hc Den)
When entered no neutron excavation corrections are made.
parameters.stated_default: calculation, enter the value here, otherwise it will be calc

parameters.name: Den Hc app
parameters.description:
'Density tool apparent hydrocarbon density' in gm/cc. If you want to override the default calculation than enter the value here otherwise it will be calculated from the HC Den parameter.
 
Default calculation depends on the Density hydrocarbon model set on the Density tab : 
 
 Conventional model : Den Hc app = RhoH * 2 (10 - 2.5 RhoH) / (16 - 2.5 RhoH)
 Modified model : Den Hc app = (5.5 * Rhohy (4-Rhohy) -3) / (16 - 2.5 RhoH) 
 
 Where RhoH is the input hydrocarbon density (Hc Den)
parameters.stated_default: calculation than enter the value here otherwise it will be c

parameters.name: Sonic Hc
parameters.description: 'Sonic hydrocarbon response' in uSec/ft. Must be entered if the Sonic porosity model is chosen.

parameters.name: PhiShr limit
parameters.description:
Volume of hydrocarbon limit seen in the flushed zone in decimals (Phi*(1-Sxo) default 0.02 . Used only in the DENSITY/NEUTRON model and with the 'variable hydrocarbon density' flag set. 
When Phi*(1-Sxo) is less than 'PhiShr limit' then the depth increment is considered to have too little hydrocarbon to accurately calculate a hydrocarbon density and the default value (Hc Den) is used.
(Parameter 22)

parameters.name: GD source
parameters.description:
'Matrix grain density source'. Options are:
 'Fixed value entered as a parameter'
 'Variable value entered as a curve' 
 'Multi-mineral'. Grain density is calculated from mineral volumes using the TRUE mineral densities.

parameters.name: Rho GD
parameters.description:
'Matrix grain density' in gm/cc. Used if the 'GD source' parameter is set to 'param'.
For the Density porosity model this is the matrix density used to calculate porosity.
For the Neutron/Density porosity model this is the starting input matrix density. If the 'variable matrix density' flag is set then this value can be different to the output matrix density.
For the Neutron porosity model this value will set neutron matrix as longs as the 'Neutron matrix value' is blank. For example, if you wanted to calculate a Neutron sandstone enter 2.65 and the non-linear neutron sandstone transform will be used.

parameters.name: Rho GD max
parameters.description: 'Matrix grain density maximum value' in gm/cc. Used only in the DENSITY/NEUTRON model and with the 'variable matrix density' flag set. This value will set the maximum possible matrix density.

parameters.name: Rho GD min
parameters.description: 'Matrix grain density minimum value' in gm/cc. Used only in the DENSITY/NEUTRON model and with the 'variable matrix density' flag set. This value will set the minimum possible matrix density.

parameters.name: Neu matrix
parameters.description:
'Neutron matrix value' in decimals porosity units. Used only in the Neutron porosity model. This is the neutron difference between 0% porosity limestone (assumed entered neutron porosity matrix) and 0% porosity of the formation matrix.
A linear response is used. Therefore if you want to convert to either sandstone or dolomite it is better to enter a value of 'Rho GD' and the non-linear transform will be used.
Any value for the 'Neu Matrix' parameter will totally override 'Rho GD', therefore if you want to use 'Rho GD' to set the neutron matrix, blank out the 'Neu Matrix' parameter.

'Neutron formation salinity correction flag'. Set to 'on' (ticked) if you want the program to make formation salinity corrections. The formation salinity correction depends on true porosity and water saturation.
If the Neutron tool has already had formation salinity corrections applied, then set this option to 'Off'(unchecked).
It is better to have the program perform the salinity correction, since it will take into account water saturation in the flushed zone.

parameters.name: Porosity Method
parameters.description:
Porosity method. Options are :
 'Neutron/Density'
 'Neutron/Sonic'
 'Neutron'

 'Input curve'. A user-selected input curve is used directly as the porosity curve. Need to set the 'Input Porosity' parameter to select 'Total' or 'Effective' porosity.

parameters.name: Variable Hc Den
parameters.description:
'Variable Hydrocarbon Density flag'. Used in the Neutron/Density porosity model. 
Set to 'On' (ticked) to calculate hydrocarbon density in the hydrocarbon zones, defined by 'PhiShr limit' parameter. Parameters 'Hc Den Min' and 'Hc Den' define the limits of the result.

parameters.name: Variable GD
parameters.description:
'Variable Matrix Grain Density' flag. Used in the Neutron/Density porosity model.
Set to 'On' (ticked) to calculate matrix density. Parameters 'Rho GD max' and 'Rho GD min' define the limits of the result.
If the 'Variable Hc Den' flag is also set, then the hydrocarbon density will be calculated first using the input matrix density. Only if the 'Hc Den' is outside its limits will the matrix density be varied.

parameters.name: Variable Vcl
parameters.description:
'Variable Clay Volume' flag. Used in the Neutron/Density porosity model.
Set to 'On' (ticked) to calculate Clay Volume. Result must be between 0 and 1.
If the 'Variable Hc Den' or 'Variable GD' flag is also set, then these will be varied first. Only if both are at their limits will the input clay volume be varied.
If 'Hc Den', 'Matrix Den' and 'Clay Vol' are all at their limits and no solution is possible then the Neutron and/or Density input curve will be reduced in order to resolve the solution given the input variables. When this happens the 'PHIFLAG' curve will be set to '6' for a reduction in density and '7' for a reduction in neutron.

parameters.name: Mineral Model
parameters.description:
'Mineral Model' option. Used in the Neutron/Density, Neutron/Sonic and Neutron porosity models and for the EPT to calculate TP matrix.
Options are :
 'Sandstone/Limestone/Dolomite'. If matrix density is greater than 2.71 than the model will be Limestone/Dolomite, less than 2.71 Sandstone/Limestone.
 'Sandstone/Dolomite'.
 'Sandstone/Special mineral'. The special mineral matrix values must be entered.
 'Limestone/Special mineral'.
 'Dolomite/special mineral'.

parameters.name: OBM ?
parameters.description:
'Oil based mud' flag. If set to 'On' (ticked) then the following logic is applied:
 Sxo must be less than or equal to Sw.
 Invasion factor logic with OBM assumes that Sxo <= Invasion factor. Therefore if the Invasion factor is set at .5 then Sxo will be the minimum of .5 or Sw.

parameters.name: Phi max
parameters.description:
'Maximum Porosity in Clean Zone' in decimal porosity units. 
 
Used to calculate Silt volume and also to limit porosity using the bad-hole logic with the 'Vcl cutoff'. 
 Silt volume is computed as VSILT = 1 - VolwetClay - Phie / PhiMax 
Also used for calculation of Shale type using the Thomas-Stieber techneque.
 Laminated / Dispersed model
 Vlam = (Vcl + Phie - PhiMax) / (1 - PhiMax)
 Vstruc = 0
 Vdisp = Vcl - Vlam
 Laminated / Structual model
 Vlam = (PhiMax - Phie) / PhiMax
 Vdisp = 0
 Vstruc = Vcl - Vlam

parameters.name: Delta Phi max
parameters.description:
'Addition to Phi Max'. Used for bad-hole with the Vcl cutoff.
If Vcl > Vcl cutoff then Phie <= (PhiMax+DeltaPhiMax)*(1.0-Vcl)*10**(-10.0*(Vcl-VclCutoff)**1.6))

parameters.name: m vari wth Vcl
parameters.description:
'Variable Cementation factor 'm' with Vcl' flag. Used for bad-hole with the Vcl cutoff.
If set to 'On' (ticked) and If Vcl > Vcl cutoff then m = m*10**(Vcl-VclCutoff). This has the effect of removing any hydrocarbons in zones of high clay content.

parameters.name: Vcl cutoff
parameters.description:
'Vclay cutoff' in decimals. Used with the following logic for bad-hole or shale zones.
If Vcl > Vcl cutoff then Phie <= (PhiMax+DeltaPhiMax)*(1.0-Vcl)*10**(-10.0*(Vcl-VclCutoff)**1.6))
If Vcl > Vcl cutoff and m variable with Vcl flag is set then m = m*10**(Vcl-VclCutoff).
If Vcl > Vcl cutoff and variable Vcl logic is chosen then VolWetClay (Vcl out) >= Vcl input.

parameters.name: Sxo Limit ?
parameters.description: 'Limit Sxo' flag. If set to 'On' (ticked) then Sxo will be limited by the equation Sxo < Sw**SxoLimit.

parameters.name: Sxo Limit
parameters.description: 'Sxo Limit exponent'. If the 'Sxo Limit' flag is set to 'On' then Sxo will be limited by the equation Sxo < Sw**SxoLimit.

parameters.name: Bad Hole Disc ?
parameters.description:
'Bad Hole Discriminator' flag. If set to 'On' (ticked) then the bad-hole discriminator logic is enabled.
If the input discriminator curve has values greater than the 'Disc Min' parameter and less than the 'Disc Max' parameter then Phie <= PhiSonic.

parameters.name: Disc Min
parameters.description:
'Discriminator Minimum' value, units of discriminator input curve. If the parameter is 'blank' then this discriminator is not used. 
If the input discriminator curve has values greater than the 'Disc Min' parameter and less than the 'Disc Max' parameter then Phie <= PhiSonic. 
If both the minimum and maximum discriminators are left 'blank', then Phie is always limited to less than PhiSonic.

parameters.name: Disc Max
parameters.description:
'Discriminator Maximum' value, units of discriminator input curve. If the parameter is left 'blank', then this discriminator is not used. 
If the input discriminator curve is greater than the 'Disc Min' parameter and less than the 'Disc Max' parameter then Phie <= PhiSonic. 
If both the minimum and maximum discriminators are 'blank' then Phie is always <= PhiSonic if the 'Bad Hole Disc' flag is turned on.

parameters.name: Sat Equation
parameters.description:
'Saturation equation'. Used both for calculation of Sxo and Sw. The following equation are available
 
 Archie 1/Rt = Phi**m.Sw**n / (a.Rw)
 Archie PhiT 1/Rt = PhiT**m.Sw**n / (a.Rw) 
 Same as Archie except PhiT used instead of Phie.
 Simandoux 1/Rt = Phi**m.Sw**n / (a.Rw) + Vcl.Sw / Rcl
 Modified Simandoux 1/Rt = Phi**m.Sw**n / (a.Rw.(1-Vcl)) + Vcl.Sw / Rcl
 Indonesian (Poupon-Leveaux) 1/Rt**.5 = ((Phi**m/(a.Rw))**.5 + Vcl**(1-Vcl/2)/Rcl**.5 ).Sw**(n/2)
 Woodhouse Tar 1/Rt**.5 = ((Phi**m/(a.Rw))**.5 + Vcl**(1-Vcl)/Rcl**.5 ).Sw**(n/2)
 Dual Water 1/Rt = PhiT**m.SwT**n/a.(1/Rw + Swb/SwT(1/Rwb-1/Rw))
 Juhasz 1/Rt = PhiT**m.SwT**n.(1+Bn.Qvn/SwT)/(a.Rw)
 Qvn = Vcl*PhiClay / PhiT
 Bn = B normalized, entered parameter
 Waxman-Smits 1/Rt = PhiT**m.SwT**n.(1+B.Qv/SwT)/(a.Rw)
 B = entered parameter or calculated from T and Rw
 Qv = a/PhiT + b where 'a' and 'b' are entered parameters. Qv can also be entered as a input curve.
 Poupon-Aguilera 1/Rt = Phi**m.Sw**n / (a.Rw(1-Vsh)) + Vsh / Rsh
 Use for Laminated clean Sand / Shale formations. Do not use if the Laminated Sw model is turned on
 Poupon-Tixier 1/Rt = (1-Vsh).Phi**m.Sw**n / (a.Rw) + Vsh / Rsh
 Use for Laminated clean Sand / Shale formations. Do not use if the Laminated Sw model is turned on

parameters.description:
Saturation model : Normal / Laminated
 
 Set to Laminated for Sw's to be calculated in the sand lamination 
In the laminated model Sw is calculated using the laminated porosity and laminated clay volume. 
 
If the Rt Lam Model is set to 'Normal' then Rt in the lamination is taken either from the entered 'Rt Lam Sand' parameter/curve or 'Rxo Lam Sand' for the flushed zone. If these parameters/curves are left blank then it is calculated from the normal Rt/Rxo entered curve and the 'Rt Lam Shale' parameter using the following formula :
 Rt Sand = (1 - Vlam) * Res * Rshale / (Rshale - Res * Vlam) 
 
 Where 
 Vlam = Volume of the shale laminations
 Res = Total resistivity of the rock
 RShale = Resistivity of shale laminations 
 
 Result is limited to 2000 ohmm 
 
If the Rt Lam Model is set to a 'Tensor' model then Rt sand is calculated from the input Tensor resistivities.
